name: Sonia Bermúdez / Gente como Uno / People Like Us cemetery

status: PERSON-BENCHMARK / HOLD, NOT CANON
work: Activist repeatedly reported as receiving or relaying distress calls from migrant boats, including in timelines of the Pylos disaster; earlier Alarm Phone material explicitly names her and her team as similar lifesaving collaborators.

name: Homeless memorial keepers / Dying Homeless and local memorial offices
location: UK / US examples; translocal office

name: Madres Buscadoras / colectivos de búsqueda (Mexico)
location: Mexico - translocal (Sonora, Veracruz, Puebla, Tamaulipas, Chiapas, Baja California and other states)
office: Search-for-the-disappeared / family-led excavation and identification / forensic refusal of erasure
status: OFFICE-CANON; NETWORK-CANDIDATE, MULTIPLE PERSON-BENCHMARKS
work: Autonomous mostly-women collectives that locate, exhume, and demand identification of people forcibly disappeared in Mexico's overlapping wars of state and cartel violence; members include Lucy Díaz Genao (Colectivo Solecitos), María Luisa Núñez Barojas (Colectivo Voz de los Desaparecidos), Cecilia Flores Armenta (Madres Buscadoras de Sonora); earlier antecedent Rosario Ibarra de Piedra (Comité Eureka, 1977); federated by MNDM coalition of ~80 groups.
why: The office is search itself - the threshold from disappeared to found alive or named dead, held open by mothers because the state's threshold is closed.
flags: At least 17 searcher-mothers murdered since 2010 with more in subsequent years; Amnesty International 2025 found 97% of buscadoras surveyed had experienced violence or harm; some collectives have negotiated cartel truces in lieu of state protection; public mythologization risks erasing those whose grief is not photogenic; cube must not aestheticize work or name specific disappeared persons; criticism of state non-search must not be flattened to partisan critique.
evidence: InSight Crime interview July 2024; Latin America Bureau February 2026 long-form; Wikipedia Madres buscadoras; Avispa Midia May 2026; AZPM February 2026; Retrospect Journal November 2025

name: Tuenjai Deetes / Hill Area Development Foundation (HADF)
location: Chiang Rai Province, northern Thailand
office: Civil-identity threshold / stateless-to-named-citizen / paperwork as anti-erasure
status: PERSON-BENCHMARK / OFFICE-CANON WITH RECOGNITION AND STATE-PROXIMITY FLAGS
work: Co-founded HADF in 1986 in Paka Sukjai village; since 1973 worked with Akha, Lahu, Lisu and other hill-tribe peoples on Thai-language education and citizenship application paperwork; helped enact 2008 Civil Registration Act amendment and 2005 Cabinet Resolution that opened naturalisation paths; over 90,000 stateless people in Thailand have acquired nationality since 2008; work continues for over 110,000 elderly stateless residents.
why: Civil identity during life - the opposite end of the cube's existing migrant-grave and name-after-death offices. Without registration, a person never becomes legally visible to any other system. Name-before-life is as severe an office as name-after-death.
flags: Former senator (2000), former NLA member (2006), former NHRC commissioner (2015-2019, resigned over investigative-power restrictions - an integrity marker), 2018 UNHCR Nansen Refugee Award Asia regional finalist; widely recognised, royal-patronage framing appears in older sources; not a fit for unknown canon, but the office is too important to omit.
evidence: USC CRCC profile; UNHCR 2018 Nansen story; Bangkok Post 2019 and October 2025; Southeast Asia Globe 2020; CTN News

name: Nyuta (Anna) Federmesser / VERA Hospice Charity Foundation / Lighthouse children's hospice (with predecessor Vera Millionschikova / First Moscow Hospice)
location: Moscow and ~60 regions of Russia; First Moscow Hospice 1994; Lighthouse children's hospice opened October 2019
office: Pain-relief threshold / palliative dignity / opioid-access at end of life
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP WITH HEAVY STATE-PROXIMITY FLAG; OFFICE-CANON FOR PAIN-RELIEF-AT-DYING
work: VERA Hospice Charity Fund founded 2006; Federmesser directs Moscow's State Center for Palliative Care from 2016; supports eight Moscow hospices and over sixty regional Russian hospices; legislative work has materially expanded opioid availability for terminally ill patients (~tenfold by some 2020 estimates after the 2016 action plan).
why: The threshold of dying without adequate pain relief is severe and non-US/UK; in Russia, doctors have feared prescribing under criminal code Article 228.2, and untreated pain has driven suicides among terminal patients. The office is morphine, prescription, refill, and the refusal to let a dying person be punished for the state's drug-policy anxiety.
flags: Federmesser joined Moscow government 2016, publicly endorsed Putin ally Sobyanin in 2018, joined All-Russia People's Front, used direct access to Putin to plead for opioid reform; critics in Russia's liberal milieu argue she has let an honest name be used by an authoritarian government; she has argued patients in pain cannot wait; after 2022 Ukraine invasion the political costs of state cooperation rose sharply. The office and outcomes are real; the entanglement is also real. DOOR-ETHICS questions remain live.
evidence: Wikipedia Anna Federmesser; SPID.center 2018 English interview; Vice/Coda 2024 long-form; ehospice government action plan; BEARR Trust

name: Bridget Tolley / Families of Sisters in Spirit (FSIS) - and broader Indigenous-led MMIWG2S+ search and memorial offices
location: Canada - Ottawa-based, translocal; office is continental
office: Indigenous-led search-for-the-disappeared / annual vigil / anti-erasure for missing and murdered Indigenous women, girls, and two-spirit people
status: KEEP WITH FAMILY-OF-VICTIM AND POLITICAL-CONTROVERSY FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON
work: Algonquin grandmother Bridget Tolley co-founded FSIS in 2011 after her mother Gladys Tolley was killed by a Sûreté du Québec police cruiser in 2001 in a death the family contests; FSIS organises annual October 4 Parliament Hill vigil; predecessor work by Native Women's Association of Canada and Beverley Jacobs's 2004 Stolen Sisters report; Jaime Black's REDress Project (2010) and Red Dress Day (May 5) parallel.
why: Search and witness for women whose disappearance falls inside settler-colonial states that have systematically declined to look. The threshold is the moment the family realises 'missing' will not become 'actively sought' without their own labour.
flags: Many founders are family-of-victim; the office cannot be cleanly separated from grief and the cube must not romanticise grief as virtue; the 2019 Reclaiming Power and Place inquiry produced 231 Calls for Justice while Indigenous-led groups continue to argue 'genocide' applies; the cube should follow Indigenous-led framing; do not publish individual victim names as proof of office.
evidence: CUPE November 2024 Sisters in Spirit vigil coverage; Assembly of First Nations MMIWG page; Canadian Museum for Human Rights resource guide; Wikipedia MMIW; National Inquiry final report site

name: Sally J. Finn / International Overdose Awareness Day (IOAD) - now stewarded by Penington Institute
location: St Kilda, Melbourne, Australia (founding 2001); now observed in 40+ countries on 31 August
office: Overdose-memorial / name-after-overdose-death / un-stigmatising grief
status: OFFICE-CANON; KEEP WITH RELIGIOUS-MOVEMENT FLAG FOR FOUNDER ORIGIN
work: Sally J. Finn, manager of a Salvation Army needle-exchange in St Kilda, began IOAD in 2001 as a small BBQ ribbon event after working with a person who had lost seventeen friends to overdose and noticing families could not openly grieve. ~6,000 silver ribbons distributed first day. Since 2012 coordinated by Penington Institute, Melbourne. Now the world's largest annual overdose-awareness campaign.
why: Parallel to the cube's NAME-AFTER-DEATH office for the unhoused: the overdose dead carry double stigma (illicit substance + 'their own fault'). The threshold is from died-of-an-illicit-cause to remembered-by-name-without-apology.
flags: Originating inside the Salvation Army programme means evangelical-organisational origin with contested LGBTQ+ record; Penington Institute steward is secular; cube should not publish family names as proof of office, and should remain alert when memorial events are co-opted into 'war on drugs' rhetoric; 'stigma reduction' is a donor claim that must be measured by bereaved families and people who use drugs, not by donor copy.
evidence: IOAD About page; SANDAS historical note; HepVu reference; Allegany Council; Weill Cornell

name: Isshinji temple (one-spirit-per-urn / Okotsubutsu practice) and Ending Center NPO (grave-friends model) - Japanese muenbotoke offices
location: Isshinji - Tennoji ward, Osaka, Japan (practice from 1887, ~decadal); Ending Center - Tokyo periphery, founded by sociologist Inoue Haruyo
office: Disconnected-dead-no-kin / muenbotoke / interment without a legal successor
status: OFFICE-CANON; INSTITUTION-CANDIDATES, NOT SINGLE-FOUNDER CANON
work: Isshinji combines cremated remains donated to the temple into a Buddha statue (Okotsubutsu) roughly once per decade, regardless of prior religious affiliation, at modest Japanese-funeral-standards fees (¥20,000-¥50,000). Ending Center is an NPO with members who pay a one-time fee, attend workshops and 'grave-friend' (haka tomo) meetings, and are interred together rather than with biological kin.
why: Japanese law and conventional Buddhist parish practice require a legal successor to maintain a family grave through ongoing fees; a person without successor becomes muenbotoke (buddha without bonds). Wealthy-aging-society counterpart to the migrant-grave office and to the cube's homeless-memorial office.
flags: Buddhist temples have a structural revenue interest in graves (the danka system); these models are partly reform of that system, not pure mercy; cherry-tree aesthetics should not substitute for analysis; the kodokushi private cleaning industry is paid commercial service rather than the costly mercy the cube studies, though workers describe the work in language much closer to mercy than to industry copy.
evidence: SSRC Immanent Frame Anne Allison 2021; Uncanny Japan podcast; Project MUSE review of Mark Rowe Bonds of the Dead; Nippon.com January 2026

name: Sudan Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs / غرف الطوارئ) - rooted in the nafir / nafeer tradition
location: Sudan - all 18 states; particularly Khartoum, Omdurman, Darfur, and Gezira
office: Collapsed-state-neighborhood-kitchen / civilian-led survival threshold during armed conflict and famine
status: OFFICE-CANON; NETWORK-CANDIDATE; KEEP WITH WAR-CONTEXT, DONOR-LEVERAGE, AND ANONYMITY FLAGS
work: Decentralised volunteer civilian-led mutual-aid networks emerged from the 2019 Resistance Committees, mobilised first against COVID-19, became Sudan's de facto humanitarian backbone after the April 2023 outbreak of war between SAF and RSF; over 11.5 million people assisted by late 2024; in Khartoum State alone ~162 base ERRs with 4,000+ volunteers running takaya community kitchens, neighbourhood clinics, evacuations, infrastructure repair, refuges for survivors of conflict-related rape; Women's Response Rooms adapt the traditional soondooq savings model.
why: The threshold is from neighbourhood-with-infrastructure to neighbourhood-the-war-wants-empty; the office is the kitchen that does not close, the clinic with a running generator, the WhatsApp room that arranges evacuation across active front lines. Mercy as horizontal mutual practice, not vertical rescue.
flags: Roughly 160 volunteers killed by late 2024; many detained, tortured, or disappeared; both warring sides routinely accuse ERRs of espionage; US declared ongoing genocide January 2025 - donor-comfort 'two sides equally to blame' framing must be resisted; ERRs themselves resist external recasting as a single charismatic organisation; cube should preserve their decentralised anonymity-protective character; international recognition (Nobel Peace Prize nomination 2025; Right Livelihood Award 2025) is now substantial - no longer unknown work but office too important to omit.
evidence: Right Livelihood laureate profile; Chatham House December 2024; The New Humanitarian 2023; Khartoum ERR self-description; Wikipedia ERRs; Mutual Aid Sudan Coalition; Upstream Journal December 2024; CMI policy brief; Giving Compass / Devex March 2026

name: Lalish rebaptism office / Yazidi Spiritual Council — Baba Sheikh Khurto Hajji Ismail (d. 2020), Khidher Domle, successor Hazim Tahsin Beg
location: Lalish temple, Sheikhan district, Duhok Governorate, Kurdistan Region of Iraq
office: Doctrinal-return-after-captivity / religious community readmission of forcibly converted and sexually enslaved survivors / anti-erasure inside the survivor's own community
status: OFFICE-CANON; INSTITUTION-CANDIDATE WITH NAMED ADVOCATES; KEEP WITH INTERNAL-LIMITS, CHILD-EXCLUSION, AND PURIFICATION-LANGUAGE FLAGS
work: September 2014 decree by Baba Sheikh declared survivors of ISIS captivity remained Yazidi and welcomed back without honour-killing or excommunication; survivors received at Lalish for rebaptism with water from the temple's holy spring; ~500 women in the first two years per Lalish elders; office continues under successor Hazim Tahsin Beg after Baba Sheikh's October 2020 death; advocate Khidher Domle (University of Dohuk) credited with brokering the doctrinal change.
why: First explicitly theological / communal-doctrinal threshold office the cube holds. Before 2014 forced conversion or rape would have meant Yazidi excommunication; the doctrinal change in the time scale of a genocide is rare. The threshold is the temple gate; the office is the rebaptism, the public welcome, the refusal to let the perpetrator's verdict become the community's.
flags: Welcome is partial — April 2019 council decree initially read as accepting children born of rape was 'clarified' three days later to exclude them, leaving Yazidi mothers and children stranded; cube holds both welcome and limit in the same entry. 'Purification' framing of rebaptism risks implying the woman, not the perpetrator, needed cleansing — noted without dismissing leaders' own framing. Do not name individual survivors as proof of office.
evidence: UNHCR profile; Foreign Policy 'A Broken Homecoming' May 2019; POMEPS 'Genocidal Rape and Community Cohesion'; Vice News rebaptism story; PRX The World May 2015; LSE Conflict Research Programme; Manara Magazine December 2023; IOM Iraq July 2025; ESM September 2025

name: Débora Maria da Silva / Mães de Maio (Mothers of May) — Brazil
location: Baixada Santista and São Paulo state, Brazil; translocal voice through Conectas Direitos Humanos
office: Mothers' refusal of impunity / memory of state-perpetrated killings / search-for-truth-and-named-victim where the killer wore the uniform
status: KEEP WITH FAMILY-OF-VICTIM AND STATE-PERPETRATOR FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR THE BRAZILIAN VARIANT OF SEARCH-FOR-THE-DISAPPEARED
work: After Crimes of May 12-21 2006 (PCC attacks followed by São Paulo Military Police and extermination-group retaliation killing 500+ civilians, overwhelmingly young Black men from peripheries), Débora and other bereaved mothers founded Mães de Maio; her son Edson Rogério Silva dos Santos, a gari, was shot dead 15 May 2006 at a gas station in Baixada Santista; 20-year anniversary marked May 2026 with extensive Brazilian press coverage; one police officer imprisoned for three deaths; work with Conectas to bring case to UN.
why: Sharpens the rev0011 SEARCH-FOR-THE-DISAPPEARED card. Where Mexican searcher-mothers face a typical cartel killer plus a non-investigating state, the Brazilian case faces uniformed state agents and allied extermination squads as the direct killers; the bodies were not missing but the cause was. The office converts grief into a public record the state will not produce.
flags: Family-of-victim founder; cube must not romanticise grief. Brazilian police violence is structural and ongoing; framing Crimes of May as exceptional understates the problem. Débora is recognised (Dandara dos Palmares, Cidadã Paulistana, Medalha Chico Mendes); not unknown-canon. Cube follows network's own 'Crimes of May' framing; does not name specific victims for aesthetic effect.
evidence: Brasil de Fato May 2026; Agência Brasil May 2026; Combate Racismo Ambiental May 2026; Jornal de Brasília on Truth Commission findings; Africas Play retrospective; Piauí Hoje on UN denunciation; Gazeta do RN profile

name: Good Nanum (좋은 나눔) / Park Jin-ok — and Nanum and Nanum (나눔과 나눔) — South Korea
location: Goyang, Seoul, and other South Korean cities; Nanum and Nanum operates the Seoul Public Funeral consultation hotline (1668-3412)
office: Disconnected-dead-no-kin in a working-age, economically-collapsed-male demographic / godoksa (고독사) funeral and naming
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP / OFFICE-CANON FOR THE KOREAN VARIANT OF DISCONNECTED-DEAD-NO-KIN
work: Good Nanum (directed by Park Jin-ok) holds one-day funerals with portrait, name tablet, Buddhist or Christian rites for people whose bodies go unclaimed at hospitals, flophouses, and police morgues; ~month-long waiting period for family to come forward; cremation and charnel-house interment. Nanum and Nanum operates Seoul's 24/7 Public Funeral consultation hotline since 2019 MOU under the 2018 Public Funeral Ordinance.
why: Korean godoksa differs from Japanese kodokushi demographically — 60% of cases are men in their 50s and 60s after job loss, disability, or post-divorce social collapse; unclaimed dead nationally nearly doubled to 6,139 in 2024. Same office shape as Japan's muenbotoke work but different threshold population; partly state-supported through civic-NGO partnership.
flags: Park Jin-ok's interview details (including a mother found with a newborn) are emotionally significant but private and not iterated as proof. Growing state involvement raises the standard state-proximity question. Visual record dominated by Jean Chung 2016 Getty Images photographs at Goyang; cube acknowledges this without endorsing image-based fundraising.
evidence: TIME 2015 profile of Park Jin-ok; CNN December 2022; CNN October 2024; Quartz background; Seoul Metropolitan Government Innovation Office page on Public Funerals

name: Crystal Paikea / Te Tai Tokerau suicide postvention team — with Fusion (Te Tai Tokerau ki Muriwhenua, 2012) and Te Arawa postvention work (Tepora Emery, Candy Cookson Cox)
location: Te Tai Tokerau / Northland, Aotearoa New Zealand; population ~179,000 in the Tai Tokerau team's catchment
office: Suicide-postvention threshold / whānau-grounded support for those bereaved by whakamomori (suicide) / indigenous reframing of stigma
status: KEEP; OFFICE-CANON FOR INDIGENOUS-LED SUICIDE POSTVENTION; TEAM-CANDIDATE WITH NAMED LEAD
work: Health New Zealand Te Whatu Ora team of three led by Crystal Paikea providing face-to-face postvention support across Te Tai Tokerau using tangi practice, whānau visits as manuhiri, kaupapa Māori method; explicitly non-clinical; works with families for years. Fusion interagency group established 2012 after 19 youth deaths in the region. Te Arawa postvention tool developed after rangatahi suicides 2008-2012. Framework: Turamarama Declaration (2017), He Tapu te Oranga o ia Tangata 2019-2024 plan.
why: Cube's first office focused on the bereaved survivor rather than the dying or the dead. Indigenous framework recovers a pre-colonial conceptualisation of suicide as whakamomori (overwhelming sadness) and kahupō (spiritual blindness) met with aroha rather than shame — the office is not reducing stigma it inherited but recovering a frame that pre-existed colonial stigma.
flags: Operates inside state health service Te Whatu Ora — inverse of the Federmesser state-proximity question (here state agency hosts indigenous-led work; office good in spite of host, not because of it). Northland youth-suicide inquest evidence indicates clinical mental health services have repeatedly failed Māori rangatahi. Suicide is cube's most sensitive topic; candidate file avoids method, specific statistics, identifying detail.
evidence: NZ Herald November 2024 on Crystal Paikea and the inquest; HQSC Fusion case study; Te Whatu Ora He Arotake review July 2024; HRC NZ on Te Arawa postvention research; Aspin et al. Kōtuitui 2024; NZ Doctor coverage of He Arotake

name: Mia Atoui / Embrace Lebanon — Embrace LifeLine 1564
location: Lebanon — Beirut-based, helpline serving the country and parts of the wider Arabic-speaking Middle East
office: Suicide-prevention hotline / psychological-distress voice / phone-that-stays-on during compounding societal collapse
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP / OFFICE-CANON FOR THE PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS LINE IN COMPOUNDING-CRISIS CONTEXT; KEEP WITH NGO-PLATFORM AND DONOR FLAGS
work: Embrace co-founded 2013 by Mia Atoui (clinical psychologist, AUB) and colleagues; 2015 crowdfunding campaign; 2017 launch of Embrace LifeLine 1564, Lebanon's first national emotional-support and suicide-prevention helpline; ~2,500 calls 2019, 6,100+ calls 2020, sharp spike after the 4 August 2020 Beirut port explosion (200+ killed, 6,000+ injured, 300,000+ displaced); two months after blast 2,239 calls of which ~67% emotional distress and ~28% suicidal ideation; line operates 12 PM to 5:30 AM toward 24/7 coverage; in-person clinic and training for first responders.
why: Cube has not held the psychological-distress threshold as such — the moment when 'still alive tomorrow' depends on who answers a phone. Lebanon since 2019 (financial collapse, COVID, port explosion, 2023-2024 Israel-Hezbollah war spillover) is the compounding-crisis case the rev0011 SearchTrail named.
flags: Relatively well-resourced NGO with international corporate partners (Facebook suicide-prevention integration); cube ordinarily prefers smaller, less platform-connected work. Closely coordinated with Lebanon Ministry of Public Health — state-proximity flag in a substantially non-functional state. Mia Atoui is a public figure (Global Thinkers Forum, IOF) more in PERSON-BENCHMARK range. Cube does not reproduce caller statistics or details about specific callers; the 1564 number is the only operational detail this entry includes.
evidence: Tahrir Institute February 2021; Embrace Lebanon team pages; Inter Press Service 2021; Foundation for Lebanon; Sarde After Dinner podcast; ReliefWeb on the helpline; Doctors Without Borders Lebanon mental-health assessment

name: Zhang Shuqin / Sun Village (太阳村) — China — refresh of rev0010 Lin Minming entry
location: Beijing (Shunyi District), Shaanxi Province (original 1996 home), and additional sites — ~9-10 Sun Village locations across China
office: Child-of-the-imprisoned / long-term residential care, schooling, prison-visit continuity, anti-stigma family contact
status: KEEP WITH PROXIMITY-TO-PRISON-SYSTEM AND DONOR-TOURISM FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR THE BETTER-DOCUMENTED CHINESE CASE OF THE CHILD-OF-THE-IMPRISONED OFFICE
work: Zhang Shuqin (former 12-year newspaper editor in China's Bureau of Prison Administration) opened the first Sun Village in Shaanxi Province in 1995-1996; network now ~9-10 group homes hosting 400-500 children whose parents are incarcerated; children attend public schools, visit parents 1-2 times/year, phone monthly; partial self-funding through orchard sales and volunteer-tourism.
why: rev0011 asked the cube to seek post-2019 non-state-media corroboration on Lin Minming / Red Apple Public Welfare. rev0012 search found none; Lin Minming sourcing remains China Daily 2018-2019 only. Sun Village has substantial independent corroboration (Dui Hua, Humanium, Harvard Fairbank Center, Beijing-kids) over a 30-year operating history. Added as the better-documented Chinese case; Lin Minming entry retained at unchanged status with the refresh result logged in REASONING-NOTE-rev0012.
flags: Zhang's prior career inside the prison administration; Sun Village must coordinate with provincial prison systems for parental contact; operates with implicit state tolerance. Independent reporting notes institutional regimes (whistles, segregated dormitories) which Chinese observers describe as ordinary boarding-school form. Volunteer-tourism arrangements (paid half-day visits on Tripadvisor) raise donor-theatre concerns. Children's identities never used as cube's evidence.
evidence: Dui Hua Foundation Issue 46; Humanium 2024/2025 update; Beijing-kids/jingkids 2014; Harvard Fairbank Center 2017; Tour Beijing profile of Zhang Shuqin; QUNO Children of Incarcerated Parents; INCCIP

name: Fatik Al-Rodaini / Mona Relief (Yemen Organization for Humanitarian Relief and Development) — Yemen
location: Sanaa-based; distributes across Yemeni governorates including Sanaa, Marib, Manakha, despite Saudi-led coalition blockade
office: Collapsed-state-neighborhood-kitchen in a blockaded country / locally-purchased food aid delivered under active bombing
status: KEEP WITH WAR-CONTEXT, BLOCKADE, AND FUNDER-DIVERSITY FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR THE YEMENI VARIANT OF COLLAPSED-STATE-NEIGHBORHOOD-KITCHEN
work: Founded 2015 by Fatik Al-Rodaini, a Sanaa-born journalist; named for the woman who made the first $1,000 donation; grew from #20ForYemen Twitter campaign ($4,200 / 150 families fed for a month) to over 7M meals distributed by 2017; all food purchased locally to circumvent blockade; team mostly Yemeni journalists/activists turned humanitarians; regular monthly food packages to Yemen's tiny remaining Jewish minority in Sanaa since 2016.

Funding from highly diverse small-donor sources (Patreon, IndieGoGo, GoFundMe) due to blockade restrictions. Al-Rodaini speaks publicly about Western complicity in the war ('Saudi money talks') — cube records this as his position. Volunteers have been targeted while delivering aid. Cube does not name individual recipients as proof of office.
evidence: Mona Relief official site; Middle East Monitor interview (Aug 2020); PRX The World 2017; CARE Yemen 2020; Alistair Reign News Blog 2015; Mona Relief media archive (Jewish community deliveries since 2016)

name: Kenya Cuevas / Casa de las Muñecas Tiresias — Casa Hogar Paola Buenrostro and successor shelters — with parallel Casa Frida and Casa Arcoíris — Mexico
location: Mexico — Casa Hogar Paola Buenrostro in CDMX (Jan 2020); Casa Hogar Catherinne Danielle Márquez in Cuernavaca, Morelos (Feb 2022); Casa Hogar Kaory Catarero Regalado in Apaxco, Estado de México (2023); parallel Casa Frida (CDMX/Tapachula/Monterrey) and Casa Arcoíris (Tijuana)
office: Chosen-family-for-trans-and-queer-adults / shelter, sober living, prison reentry, legal/identity advocacy for trans women, gay men, and queer migrants
status: KEEP WITH FAMILY-OF-VICTIM, RECOGNITION, AND CULT-OF-PERSONALITY FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR CHOSEN-FAMILY-FOR-TRANS-AND-QUEER-ADULTS
work: Kenya Cuevas — trans woman, sex worker, survivor of prison, addiction, HIV diagnosis — founded the network after the 30 September 2016 murder of her friend Paola Buenrostro in CDMX's La Merced. Casa Hogar Paola Buenrostro opened January 2020 as Mexico's first dedicated shelter for trans women; network now spans three houses. Work includes prison legal-literacy workshops for trans women, post-release pickup and integration. Served ~1,800 (2018, pre-shelter) and ~10,000 (2020). Casa Frida (founded May 2020) served 423 LGBTIQ+ refugees and reintegrated 349 by early 2024.
why: rev0012 SearchTrail named trans chosen-family work without naming minors. These shelters are the right shape — adults, named at their own names, reconnected when biological families and the Mexican state have failed them.
flags: Latin America accounts for ~70% of global registered trans murders. Cuevas has received significant international recognition (2022 Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Award) — public-figure visibility flag. Leadership has been described as personalistic; successor question not yet resolved. Shelters partly funded through CDMX government and corporate donations — standard state-proximity DOOR-ETHICS question. Mixed user reviews note administrative friction. Residents not named as proof of office.
evidence: Washington Blade 2021; Casa Frida website; GIRE/Karen Villalobos Feb 2024; El Diario.es Feb 2022; Homosensual Jan 2024; Agencia Presentes Dec 2021; USF Master's Thesis 2024

name: Pastor Nelson Moz / Eben-Ezer Baptist Church and Pastor Nestor Cruz / Hungry Church — El Salvador (with companion person-benchmark canon Greg Boyle / Homeboy Industries)
location: San Salvador and elsewhere in El Salvador; particularly evangelical churches in former MS-13 and Barrio 18 territories
office: Religious exit-ramp / reentry-from-gang via faith community / the rare departure from a gang the gang will permit
status: KEEP WITH STATE-OF-EMERGENCY ENDANGERMENT, EVANGELICAL-FRAMING, AND CONVERSION-AS-PRECONDITION FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR THE NON-US PARALLEL TO HOMEBOY INDUSTRIES
work: In El Salvador gangs do not let members 'retire'; departure typically means death. The two near-universal exceptions are emigration and conversion to an evangelical church. Pastor Nelson Moz has led Eben-Ezer Baptist Church in San Salvador for 20+ years, surviving multiple police raids during worship under the post-2022 state of emergency. Pastor Nestor Cruz founded Hungry Church for MS-13-affiliated deportees returning to El Salvador after US prison; provides housing, microbusiness (eggs, pupusas), and from 2018 carpentry/auto-mechanics training partly funded through Salvadoran Lutheran Church/ELCA. Research by José Miguel Cruz (FIU) finds >50% of surveyed Salvadoran gang members identify as evangelical.
why: rev0012 SearchTrail named 'prison reentry beyond the US' specifically. The Salvadoran and Honduran evangelical reentry offices are the most documented non-US case of the gang/prison reentry office and the most endangered — pastors arrested under Bukele's March 2022 state of emergency.
flags: Conversion as precondition: the gang surveils former members for visible church attendance, sobriety, and avoidance of crime; will kill a member who 'fails as a Christian.' Cube notes this without endorsing evangelical-only framing. Bukele state-of-emergency arrests have undone years of pastoral reinsertion work. Some sources withhold pastors' real names; cube uses names already public and does not name individuals at risk. Greg Boyle / Homeboy Industries kept as PERSON-BENCHMARK only (too famous, US-centric).
evidence: CSM Sep 2017; CPR/NPR Jul 2018; Newsweek Sep 2019; America Magazine Apr 2022; Grand Canyon Synod ELCA on Hungry Church; Amnesty International Aug 2022; Conciliation Resources on 2012 truce; UMNews on Honduras pastoral work

name: Marius Romme, Sandra Escher, Patsy Hage / Hearing Voices Movement / Intervoice — translocal
location: Origin Maastricht, Netherlands (1987); now Intervoice and national Hearing Voices Networks in ~29 countries
office: Peer-led psychiatric crisis support / non-pathologising frame for voice-hearing / refusal of the medical model as the only model
status: OFFICE-CANON; FOUNDER-PLUS-VOICE-HEARER NETWORK CANDIDATE; KEEP WITH DECEASED-PROFESSOR, ACADEMIC-PROXIMITY, AND MEDICATION-DEBATE FLAGS
work: 1987 Dutch TV appeal by Romme (psychiatrist), Escher (journalist/child psychologist), and Hage (voice-hearer) drew hundreds of voice-hearer responses; formed the basis of the movement. Premises: voice-hearing is a meaningful human experience (~2-4% of population hears voices without psychiatric contact); voices best understood in trauma/life context; peer support is essential. UK network founded 1988 (Manchester). Intervoice incorporated as UK not-for-profit 2007, Romme president until his 2021 death. SAMHSA 'promising practice' designation. Successor leadership includes Jacqui Dillon, Eleanor Longden, Dirk Corstens, Mark Morris.
why: rev0012 SearchTrail named psychiatric peer-support. Open Dialogue (Western Lapland) is a state public-health system, wrong shape for cube. Hearing Voices Movement is the peer-led counterpart — Hearing Voices Groups in living rooms and church halls before earning their place in policy.
flags: Romme was a psychiatry professor — office not strictly 'unknown canon' though groups themselves are peer-led. Uneasy relationship with mainstream psychiatric research methods. Some clinicians remain critical; cube does not adjudicate clinical dispute. Movement does not require non-medication but has at times read as anti-medication. Individual voice-hearers not named or described as proof of office beyond their own self-chosen testimony in published research.
evidence: Tandfonline Living Tribute to Romme (2022); Schizophrenia Bulletin (Corstens et al. 2014); Hearing Voices Network UK; Intervoice; Hearing Voices Network USA; Understanding Voices; Lancet Psychiatry 2015; Wikipedia

location: Calais, Grande-Synthe, Dunkirk, northern France / UK-France border

status: OFFICE-CANON; NETWORK-CANDIDATE; KEEP WITH BORDER-CRIMINALISATION, NGO-VISIBILITY, AND IMAGE-RISK FLAGS
